title: Two complete training passes retain checkpoint three as the provisional choice

data.title: Two complete training passes retain checkpoint three as the provisional choice
paragraphs: At update 589,480, two complete passes have finished and the fourth of six native development comparisons passes every frozen numerical guard. Equal-weight nine-cohort WER is 17.684%, versus 18.511% for the preserved initial model, an absolute improvement of 0.827 percentage points. It is 0.281 points worse than checkpoint 442,110 at 17.402%. Seven cohorts improve and two regress relative to initial. The saved summary therefore retains step 442,110 as the provisional best eligible checkpoint. Selection remains unfinished until all six comparisons complete, and the initial model remains default.

The checkpoint records 4,105,502 training-view visits: every one of the 2,052,751 qualified views has been visited twice. Visits/distinct sources are Common Voice 182,246/91,123; AMI 1,365,624/76,795; CHiME-6 2,523,774/51,743; and VOiCES 33,858/513. The pool still represents 220,174 distinct source utterances rather than millions of independent utterances. Full-parameter training, the original four-domain objective weights, source balance, quiet-view confidence and exclusion of development/evaluation remain unchanged.

Noisy and age cohort WER: AMI 26.825% to 25.035% (-1.790 percentage points; saved 95% change interval [-4.759, +0.621]); CHiME-6 76.320% to 72.252% (-4.068 percentage points; saved 95% change interval [-9.249, +0.650]); Common Voice age 12.286% to 12.368% (+0.081 percentage points; saved 95% change interval [-1.753, +1.836]). AMI and CHiME-6 remain better than initial in aggregate but are worse than checkpoint three; Common Voice age remains slightly worse than initial.

Clean and native WER: CMU Arctic clean 8.541% to 8.185% (-0.356 percentage points; saved 95% change interval [-1.381, +0.547]); HiFiTTS clean 7.485% to 7.022% (-0.463 percentage points; saved 95% change interval [-0.749, -0.262]); HiFiTTS native 6.464% to 6.160% (-0.304 percentage points; saved 95% change interval [-1.039, +0.369]). The HiFiTTS clean interval excludes zero but is fragile with only two development readers; HiFiTTS native has only four. This limited coverage does not establish broad improvement.

LibriSpeech and VOiCES WER: LibriSpeech clean 5.894% to 5.975% (+0.081 percentage points; saved 95% change interval [-0.763, +0.983]); LibriSpeech native 10.269% to 10.224% (-0.045 percentage points; saved 95% change interval [-1.249, +1.025]); VOiCES 12.511% to 11.932% (-0.579 percentage points; saved 95% change interval [-1.535, +0.364]). The Common Voice age and LibriSpeech clean point-estimate regressions both remain within the frozen guards. VOiCES remains sparsely covered by 26 source utterances, 78 microphone views and 13 speakers.

The saved 10,000-draw paired cluster-bootstrap interval for the candidate-minus-initial nine-cohort WER change is [-1.553, -0.161] percentage points. The aggregate interval is below zero, while all cohort intervals except the two-reader HiFiTTS clean interval include zero. This interval compares checkpoint four with initial, not with checkpoint three, so it does not establish that the 0.281-point difference between checkpoints is reliable. The bootstrap averages microphone views per source and resamples meetings, sessions or speakers; its exploratory development intervals are not adjusted for choosing among six checkpoints.

Microphone slices show a renewed CHiME-6 worn-microphone regression: initial WER 41.606% rises to 48.905% on 27 clips, a 7.299-point increase; checkpoint three was 42.336%. CHiME-6 array remains better than initial, 79.212% to 74.864%, which masks the worn-slice problem in the aggregate. AMI array improves from 31.859% to 30.540% and headset from 17.804% to 15.430%, although both are worse than checkpoint three. These slices have no saved slice-specific intervals. They inform interpretation without overriding the frozen cohort-based decision.

Quiet-speech WER rises from 31.823% to 32.146%, a 0.324-point regression on 160 views, 77 sources and 1,004 reference words. The saved 95% change interval is [-2.993, +4.561] points. Its point estimate passes the 1.0-point guard, but quiet-speech improvement is not established. Both initial and checkpoint four produce zero false positives and zero inserted words on the 20 silence/noise probes; that limited probe set does not establish product-microphone performance.

The pipeline has begun its third and final training pass toward update 736,850. Two fixed comparisons remain before one development candidate is frozen; confirmation will not choose a runner-up. Both panels reuse previously evaluated populations and provide no fresh independent confirmation. The one-reader HiFiTTS clean confirmation interval and the complete nine-cohort confirmation interval remain undefined rather than certain. Real product-microphone validation and an independent final age test remain absent. All new checkpoints remain experimental and the preserved initial model remains default.
